2.title: Table Position: Where You Sit Changes Everything
2.subtitle: Position is the most underrated concept in poker. It determines how much information you have before you act.

content.intro: In Texas Hold'em, players act in a fixed order every street. Acting later means you've seen what everyone else does first — that information is enormously powerful preflop.

positions.name: Small Blind
positions.description: You post half the big blind and act first on every postflop street. You have the worst position at the table.
positions.preflop_advice: Play tight. You're forced to put money in, but you'll be out of position all hand long.
positions.playable_hands: Premium hands only: AA, KK, QQ, JJ, AK

positions.name: Big Blind
positions.description: You post the full blind and act last preflop. You get a discount to continue — but you'll be out of position postflop.
positions.preflop_advice: Defend wider than SB since you're already invested, but don't go overboard.
positions.playable_hands: Wider defense range: any pair, suited connectors, A-x suited

positions.name: Under the Gun
positions.description: First to act preflop. You have zero information about what anyone else will do.
positions.preflop_advice: Play the tightest range from here. Your hand needs to be strong enough to handle raises from anyone behind you.
positions.playable_hands: AA, KK, QQ, JJ, TT, AK, AQs

positions.name: Middle Position
positions.description: A few players have acted, a few are still left to act. Moderate information, moderate position.
positions.preflop_advice: You can open slightly wider than UTG, but still stick to solid hands.
positions.playable_hands: Add: 99, 88, AJ, KQ, suited connectors like JTs

positions.name: Cutoff
positions.description: One seat before the button. You have good position — only the button acts after you.
positions.preflop_advice: Open fairly wide here. You'll have position against the blinds if they call.
positions.playable_hands: Add: 77, 66, A-x suited, KJ, QJ, broadways

positions.name: Button
positions.description: The best seat at the table. You act last on every postflop street — a massive advantage.
positions.preflop_advice: Open the widest range from here. You can profitably play many more hands when you always act last.
positions.playable_hands: Expand to: 55, 44, any suited ace, Kx suited, weak broadways, suited connectors down to 65s

content.core_rule: The later you act, the more hands you can profitably play.

2.key_takeaway: Early position = tight ranges. Late position = wide ranges. The button is the most profitable seat — use it.

1.title: Preflop Hand Strength
1.subtitle: Not all starting hands are created equal. Learn which hands are strong, which are speculative, and which to fold.

content.intro: Your two hole cards determine your preflop options. Hand strength isn't just about the absolute value of your cards — it's about how they interact with position, stack size, and the action in front of you.

tiers.label: Premium
tiers.description: The best starting hands in poker. Raise or re-raise from any position. These hands play well in big pots.
tiers.tip: With AA and KK, you want to build the pot preflop. Don't slowplay — raise big.

tiers.label: Strong
tiers.description: Very strong hands that play well from most positions. Open-raise from middle position onwards, and 3-bet vs. loose openers.
tiers.action: Raise from MP+, call or 3-bet vs. opens
tiers.tip: TT and 99 are strong but vulnerable to overcards on the flop. Position matters a lot with these.

tiers.label: Playable
tiers.description: Solid hands in position. From the cutoff or button, these are opens. From early position, proceed with caution.
tiers.action: Open from CO/BTN, consider from MP
tiers.tip: Suited hands like ATs and JTs gain value from flush draw potential — they play better than their off-suit equivalents.

tiers.label: Speculative
tiers.description: These hands need the right conditions: late position, good pot odds, or a cheap flop. Don't over-invest preflop.
tiers.action: Open from BTN only, call in position with good odds
tiers.tip: Small pairs are set-mining hands — you're hoping to flop three-of-a-kind. It won't happen often, so you need a good price to see the flop.

tiers.label: Fold (mostly)
tiers.description: The majority of hands you're dealt. Folding is profitable. Don't fall in love with cards just because they're yours.
tiers.tip: Beginners play too many hands. The best preflop decision is often folding and waiting for a better spot.

key_factors.label: Suitedness
key_factors.detail: Suited hands (same suit) are worth more — they can make flushes. AKs is stronger than AKo.

key_factors.label: Connectivity
key_factors.detail: Connected cards (like JT, 98) can make straights, adding hidden value on the right boards.

key_factors.label: Position
key_factors.detail: A hand that's a fold UTG can be a profitable open from the button. Always adjust for where you're sitting.

1.key_takeaway: Premium hands play themselves. With everything else, your position at the table determines whether the hand is worth playing at all.

1.question: You're Under the Gun (UTG). Which hand should you fold?
options: AA
KK
87 suited
AK
1.explanation: 87 suited is a speculative hand that needs position and good odds to be profitable. From UTG — the tightest position — it's a clear fold.

2.question: You're on the Button. Compared to UTG, you should play...
options: Tighter — more players can act behind you
The same range — position doesn't matter preflop
Wider — you'll act last postflop and have more info
Wider — but only if you have a pair
2.explanation: The Button acts last on every postflop street, which is a huge informational advantage. You can profitably play far more hands from here.

3.question: Why are suited hands (e.g. AKs) better than off-suit hands (e.g. AKo)?
options: They're easier to remember
They can make flushes, adding extra ways to win
Suits don't actually matter preflop
They always make a pair on the flop
3.explanation: Suited hands gain value from the possibility of making a flush. AKs has roughly 3-4% more equity than AKo because of this.

4.question: Which position acts FIRST preflop?
options: Button
Big Blind
Small Blind
Under the Gun
4.explanation: Under the Gun (UTG) is first to act preflop because the blinds have already posted. This forces UTG to play with no information — hence the tight range.

5.question: You have 55 (a small pair). Which is the best situation to play it?
options: UTG, raise big to win the blinds
Button, call a small open to try to flop a set
Big Blind, 3-bet all-in against a UTG raise
Fold it — small pairs are never worth playing
5.explanation: Small pairs are set-mining hands. You want to see a cheap flop in position hoping to flop three-of-a-kind. Calling a small open from the button is the ideal spot.
